correctness.rationale: The excess-outdegree identity leaves only one-branch and two-branch cases. First-return Perron equations are exact. Sharp exponent-transfer inequalities settle the one-branch case and force the stated roses at equality; a complete three-pattern analysis of the two-branch first-return matrix is strict at both candidate roots.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. Klech arXiv:2609.18367 states the two formulas as Conjecture 5.15. Exact-formula, tricyclic-digraph, fixed-arc-excess and related-family searches found no prior proof of the full conjecture. The source is extremely recent, so unindexed parallel work remains a residual risk.

value.rationale: The result proves both parts of an explicit current conjecture, determines all equality cases, and replaces a large family comparison by a short branching-excursion Perron reduction that may extend to other small fixed arc excesses.

disclaimer: Not independent validation, peer review, or a guarantee of first discovery.
